cases.sentence: Гость внимательно посмотрел и внушительно произнес: Петр Петрович ___.
cases.translation: The guest looked attentively and said impressively: Pyotr Petrovich Luzhin.
cases.explain: «Лужин» stands in apposition to the implied subject «я» (I am), so it takes the nominative case.

cases.translation: Razumikhin pulled his chair back from the table.
cases.explain: The preposition «от» (away from) governs the genitive case, giving «стола».

cases.sentence: Не обеспокою ли я больного своим присутствием? — обратился Петр Петрович к ___.
cases.translation: "Won't I be troubling the patient with my presence?" Pyotr Petrovich turned to Zosimov.
cases.explain: The preposition «к» (toward) governs the dative case, giving «Зосимову».

cases.translation: Razumikhin laid the promissory note on the table.
cases.explain: «Выложил» (laid out) is a transitive verb whose direct object takes the accusative case, giving «письмо».

cases.sentence: Раскольников лежал бледный, с вздрагивающей верхнею ___.
cases.translation: Raskolnikov lay pale, his upper lip trembling.
cases.explain: The instrumental case here describes the accompanying feature («с» + instrumental), giving «губой».

cases.sentence: Он остановился в ___, озираясь кругом с обидно-нескрываемым удивлением.
cases.translation: He stopped in the doorway, looking around with an insultingly undisguised astonishment.
cases.explain: The preposition «в» marking location governs the prepositional case, giving «дверях» (the plural form used for "doorway").

reading.ru: Это был господин немолодых уже лет, чопорный, осанистый, с осторожною и брюзгливою физиономией, который начал тем, что остановился в дверях, озираясь кругом с обидно-нескрываемым удивлением и как будто спрашивая взглядами
reading.question: How is the newly arrived guest first described?
options: A prim, portly, no-longer-young gentleman with a cautious, fretful expression
reading.correct: A prim, portly, no-longer-young gentleman with a cautious, fretful expression
reading.explain: He is described as no longer young, prim, portly, with a cautious and fretful face.

reading.ru: — Родион Романыч Раскольников, господин студент или бывший студент?
reading.question: What does the visitor first ask upon entering?
options: Whether the man before him is Rodion Romanovich Raskolnikov
Whether this is the right apartment number
reading.correct: Whether the man before him is Rodion Romanovich Raskolnikov
reading.explain: He formally asks whether he is addressing Rodion Romanovich Raskolnikov, student or former student.

reading.ru: — А вот он лежит на диване! А вам что нужно?
reading.question: How does Razumikhin rudely respond to the visitor's formal question?
options: He bluntly points out Raskolnikov and asks what the visitor wants
He apologizes profusely for Raskolnikov's condition
He asks the visitor to leave immediately
reading.correct: He bluntly points out Raskolnikov and asks what the visitor wants
reading.explain: Razumikhin answers with blunt familiarity, pointing out Raskolnikov on the sofa and asking what the visitor needs.

reading.ru: — Петр Петрович Лужин. Я в полной надежде, что имя мое не совсем уже вам безызвестно.
reading.question: How does the visitor introduce himself?
options: As Pyotr Petrovich Luzhin, hoping his name is not entirely unknown to Raskolnikov
reading.correct: As Pyotr Petrovich Luzhin, hoping his name is not entirely unknown to Raskolnikov
reading.explain: He introduces himself as Pyotr Petrovich Luzhin, expressing hope his name is already known to Raskolnikov.

reading.ru: Но Раскольников, ожидавший чего-то совсем другого, тупо и задумчиво посмотрел на него и ничего не ответил, как будто имя Петра Петровича слышал он решительно в первый раз.
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov react to hearing Luzhin's name?
options: He stares blankly, as if hearing the name for the first time
He immediately recognizes and greets him warmly
reading.correct: He stares blankly, as if hearing the name for the first time
reading.explain: Raskolnikov, expecting something else entirely, stares blankly as though hearing Pyotr Petrovich's name for the very first time.

reading.ru: Я предполагал и рассчитывал, — замямлил он, — что письмо, пущенное уже с лишком десять дней, даже чуть ли не две недели…
reading.question: What does Luzhin assume regarding a letter about him?
options: That Raskolnikov should have already received it more than ten days ago
That the letter was never sent
That Raskolnikov's mother refused to write it
That the letter was addressed to someone else
reading.correct: That Raskolnikov should have already received it more than ten days ago
reading.explain: He mumbles that he assumed the letter, sent more than ten days—almost two weeks—ago, would have already reached Raskolnikov.

reading.ru: Знаю, знаю! — проговорил вдруг Раскольников, с выражением самой нетерпеливой досады. — Это вы? Жених? Ну, знаю!.. и довольно!
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov finally respond once he realizes who Luzhin is?
options: With impatient irritation, identifying him as "the fiancé" and cutting him off
With complete confusion, asking who he is again
reading.correct: With impatient irritation, identifying him as "the fiancé" and cutting him off
reading.explain: Raskolnikov cuts him off impatiently, recognizing him as "the fiancé" and saying that's enough.

reading.ru: Даже щегольская, новехонькая, круглая шляпа об этой цели свидетельствовала: Петр Петрович как-то уж слишком почтительно с ней обращался и слишком осторожно держал ее в руках.
reading.question: What detail about Luzhin's hat reveals his eagerness to impress as a bridegroom?
options: He handles his brand-new hat with excessive, self-conscious care
He refuses to remove his hat indoors
He wears an old, battered hat
reading.correct: He handles his brand-new hat with excessive, self-conscious care
reading.explain: His stylish, brand-new round hat betrays his purpose, as he handles it with excessive respect and caution.

reading.ru: Лицо его, весьма свежее и даже красивое, и без того казалось моложе своих сорока пяти лет.
reading.question: How old is Luzhin, according to the narrator, despite looking younger?
reading.correct: Forty-five
reading.explain: The narrator states his face looked younger than his forty-five years.

reading.ru: Ваша мамаша, еще в бытность мою при них, начала к вам письмо.
reading.question: What does Luzhin say about Raskolnikov's mother and a letter?
options: That she began writing him a letter while Luzhin was still with her
That she asked Luzhin not to visit
That she has stopped writing to him entirely
That she sent Luzhin instead of writing
reading.correct: That she began writing him a letter while Luzhin was still with her
reading.explain: Luzhin explains that Raskolnikov's mother had begun a letter to him while Luzhin was still staying with the family.

reading.ru: Весьма недалеко отсюда, дом Бакалеева…
reading.question: Where has Luzhin arranged temporary lodging for Raskolnikov's mother and sister?
options: Bakaleev's house, not far from Raskolnikov
reading.correct: Bakaleev's house, not far from Raskolnikov
reading.explain: Luzhin says he has found them lodging at Bakaleev's house, quite close by.

reading.ru: Скверность ужаснейшая: грязь, вонь, да и подозрительное место; штуки случались; да и черт знает кто не живет!..
reading.question: How does Razumikhin describe the lodging house Luzhin arranged?
options: As a dirty, foul-smelling, suspicious place with scandalous incidents
As too expensive for ordinary people
reading.correct: As a dirty, foul-smelling, suspicious place with scandalous incidents
reading.explain: Razumikhin calls it a terrible, filthy, foul-smelling, suspicious place where scandalous things have happened.

reading.ru: Да, Андрей Семеныч Лебезятников, служащий в министерстве. Изволите знать?
reading.question: Who is Andrei Semyonovich Lebezyatnikov, according to Luzhin?
options: A young civil servant and Luzhin's former ward, now his friend
reading.correct: A young civil servant and Luzhin's former ward, now his friend
reading.explain: Luzhin identifies him as a young man serving in a ministry, whom he was once the guardian of.

reading.ru: Я, видите ли, уже десять лет не посещал Петербурга.
reading.question: How long has Luzhin been away from Petersburg, by his own account?
reading.correct: Ten years
reading.explain: He states he has not visited Petersburg for ten years.

reading.ru: Врешь ты, деловитости нет, — вцепился Разумихин. — Деловитость приобретается трудно, а с неба даром не слетает.
reading.question: How does Razumikhin respond to Luzhin's claim that the younger generation shows more "business sense"?
options: He flatly contradicts him, saying real competence is hard-won, not a gift from the sky
He changes the subject to the murder case
He asks Zosimov to settle the argument
reading.correct: He flatly contradicts him, saying real competence is hard-won, not a gift from the sky
reading.explain: Razumikhin bluntly disagrees, insisting that genuine competence is hard to acquire and doesn't fall from the sky for free.

reading.ru: Наука же говорит: возлюби, прежде всех, одного себя, ибо всё на свете на личном интересе основано.
reading.question: What economic/philosophical theory does Luzhin expound at length?
options: That one should love oneself first, since everything rests on self-interest
That charity should be the highest virtue
That the state should control all property
That love for one's neighbor comes before all else
reading.correct: That one should love oneself first, since everything rests on self-interest
reading.explain: Luzhin argues that "science" teaches one should love oneself above all, since everything in the world rests on personal interest.

reading.ru: Извините, я тоже неостроумен, — резко перебил Разумихин, — а потому перестанемте.
reading.question: How does Razumikhin cut off Luzhin's lengthy theorizing?
options: He sharply interrupts, sarcastically claiming he too lacks wit, so they should stop
He politely asks him to continue
He falls asleep out of boredom
reading.correct: He sharply interrupts, sarcastically claiming he too lacks wit, so they should stop
reading.explain: Razumikhin interrupts sharply, sarcastically saying he too is "not witty," so they should stop the discussion.

reading.ru: Убил непременно закладчик? — утвердительно говорил Зосимов.
reading.question: What theory does Zosimov assert about who committed the murders?
options: That it must have been a pawnbroker (someone who pawned items)
That it was a random stranger
That the old woman killed herself
reading.correct: That it must have been a pawnbroker (someone who pawned items)
reading.explain: Zosimov states as if certain that the murderer must have been one of the people who had pawned items with the old woman.

reading.ru: Это, кажется, о недавнем убийстве старухи чиновницы, — вмешался, обращаясь к Зосимову, Петр Петрович, уже стоя со шляпой в руке и перчатками
reading.question: What topic does Luzhin insert himself into just before leaving?
options: The recent murder of the old pawnbroker woman
The economics of the younger generation
The rent for his new apartment
reading.correct: The recent murder of the old pawnbroker woman
reading.explain: Luzhin interjects, addressing Zosimov, about the recent murder of the old official's widow (the pawnbroker).

reading.ru: А доведите до последствий, что вы давеча проповедовали, и выйдет, что людей можно резать…
reading.question: What accusation does Raskolnikov suddenly level against Luzhin's theory?
options: That taken to its logical conclusion, it justifies killing people
That it contradicts Christian teaching only
That it was stolen from another thinker
reading.correct: That taken to its logical conclusion, it justifies killing people
reading.explain: Raskolnikov argues that if you follow Luzhin's theory to its logical conclusion, it would justify "cutting people's throats."

reading.ru: А то, что если вы еще раз… осмелитесь упомянуть хоть одно слово… о моей матери… то я вас с лестницы кувырком спущу!
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov threaten to do if Luzhin mentions his mother again?
options: Throw him down the stairs head over heels
reading.correct: Throw him down the stairs head over heels
reading.explain: Raskolnikov threatens that if Luzhin dares mention his mother again, he will throw him tumbling down the stairs.

reading.ru: А, так вот оно что-с! — Лужин побледнел и закусил губу.
reading.question: How does Luzhin react physically to Raskolnikov's threat?
options: He turns pale and bites his lip
He storms out immediately without a word
reading.correct: He turns pale and bites his lip
reading.explain: Luzhin turns pale and bites his lip in reaction to the threat.

reading.ru: Оставьте, оставьте меня все! — в исступлении вскричал Раскольников. — Да оставите ли вы меня наконец, мучители!
reading.question: What does Raskolnikov cry out after Luzhin finally leaves?
options: For everyone to leave him alone, calling them tormentors
For someone to bring him food
For Razumikhin to fetch his mother
For Zosimov to give him more medicine
reading.correct: For everyone to leave him alone, calling them tormentors
reading.explain: In a frenzy, Raskolnikov shouts for everyone to leave him alone, calling them his tormentors.

reading.ru: Если бы только толчок ему какой-нибудь благоприятный, вот бы чего! Давеча он был в силах… Знаешь, у него что-то есть на уме!
reading.question: What does Zosimov say he fears about Raskolnikov's mental state, once outside?
options: That something fixed and oppressive is weighing on his mind
That he will die from his fever
That he is faking his illness
reading.correct: That something fixed and oppressive is weighing on his mind
reading.explain: Zosimov says he fears there's something fixed and weighing on Raskolnikov's mind that troubles him deeply.

reading.ru: После! Я спать хочу! Оставь меня…
reading.question: How does Raskolnikov respond when Nastasya asks if he wants tea, at the very end of the chapter?
options: He refuses, saying he wants to sleep, and turns convulsively to the wall as she leaves
He asks her to stay and talk
He falls asleep before she can ask
reading.correct: He refuses, saying he wants to sleep, and turns convulsively to the wall as she leaves
reading.explain: He tells her he wants to sleep instead, and turns convulsively to the wall as she leaves the room.
